primaryQuery: will a smart thermostat work without internet
readerQuestion: If my internet service goes down, will my heat or air conditioning keep running, and which thermostat features or Home Assistant controls will stop?
selectedBecause: The same practical reliability question recurs across Reddit and Home Assistant Community discussions from 2021 through 2026. Current results usually collapse internet, Wi-Fi, Home Assistant, and utility-power failures into one generic answer or cover only one brand. A source-backed failure matrix is durable, useful to a homeowner before and after purchase, and distinct from Tara's existing thermostat buying guide when it stays focused on outage behavior rather than product ranking.

demandSignals.evidence: A homeowner asks for a thermostat that does not require external internet access, and replies distinguish cloud-dependent control from Z-Wave and local HomeKit paths.
A 2026 discussion revisits whether the thermostat's own controls and schedule remain usable when Home Assistant or internet access is unavailable.
The reader wants standalone thermostat management on the home network, reflecting the recurring need to separate basic HVAC operation from a vendor cloud.

A current ecobee integration report illustrates that a web-login or token path can fail independently of the thermostat's basic wall operation; it is architecture evidence, not a claim that all ecobee units share the reported fault.

The exact-query results are mostly generic HVAC explainers or single-brand answers. They tend to say that basics continue without separating internet loss from router loss, Home Assistant loss, or utility-power loss.

searchReview.query: will a smart thermostat work without internet
searchReview.intent: The searcher wants to know whether heating or cooling remains safe and controllable during an internet outage and exactly which wall, schedule, app, voice, and automation features stop.
searchReview.resultGap: Reviewed results generally offer an oversimplified yes or discuss one brand. They rarely distinguish a WAN outage from Wi-Fi/router failure, Home Assistant downtime, or loss of HVAC power, and they seldom map exact official cloud and local control paths to what still works.

officialSources.name: Google Nest thermostat offline help
officialSources.supports: A disconnected Nest thermostat can still be adjusted at the wall, while app control is unavailable; power and battery loss are separate reconnection issues.

officialSources.name: Google Nest thermostat software history
officialSources.supports: Matter support is model-specific: the 2020 Nest Thermostat and the fourth-generation Nest Learning Thermostat have different documented Matter capabilities.

officialSources.name: Sensi Wi-Fi outage support
officialSources.supports: Heating, cooling, and the current schedule continue during a lost Wi-Fi connection, while geofencing, advanced settings, schedule changes, and updates wait for reconnection.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant internet outage FAQ
officialSources.supports: Local protocols can operate without internet, while integrations that depend on an external cloud cannot reach that cloud during an outage.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant ecobee integration
officialSources.supports: The official ecobee integration is classified as Cloud Polling.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant Google Nest integration
officialSources.supports: The official Nest integration uses Google's Smart Device Management and Pub/Sub services and is classified as Cloud Push.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant Venstar integration
officialSources.supports: Supported Venstar ColorTouch and Explorer models use Local Polling and do not require the Skyport cloud for Home Assistant control.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant HomeKit Device integration
officialSources.supports: A supported climate accessory paired through HomeKit Device uses Local Push and may expose fewer settings than a vendor integration.

officialSources.name: ecobee Smart Thermostat Premium product documentation
officialSources.supports: The current Smart Thermostat Premium officially supports Apple HomeKit; combined with Home Assistant's HomeKit Device documentation, this supports the model-specific local pairing path.

officialSources.name: ecobee Smart Thermostat Enhanced product documentation
officialSources.supports: The current Smart Thermostat Enhanced officially supports Apple HomeKit; combined with Home Assistant's HomeKit Device documentation, this supports the model-specific local pairing path.

officialSources.name: Resideo T6 Pro Z-Wave product documentation
officialSources.supports: The TH6320ZW2007/U is a programmable Z-Wave thermostat with configurable 7-day, 5-1-1, and 5-2 scheduling.

officialSources.name: tado X offline operation instructions
officialSources.supports: Offline installation and operation are model- and topology-specific for tado X devices, so generic brand-level promises are unsafe.

existingCoverage.decision: The proposed URL owns thermostat outage behavior: what happens at the wall and through each control path when internet service, the router, Home Assistant, or HVAC power fails. The existing thermostat article continues to own product selection, the no-cloud article owns the broad architecture question, the downtime article owns controller failure, and the Matter and tado X articles own their protocol- and product-specific setup details. /smart-thermostat-kit/ remains the sole commercial owner. The new article avoids rankings and close buying-guide variations and links those owners descriptively.
